claim:
Text: "People who do not vote for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the 2020 elections will not get the COVID vaccine free of cost."
Claim author: Firoz Khan 
Claim date: October 22, 2020
Claim origin: https://twitter.com/sirfirozkhan/status/1319360671729922048
before_justification: The fact-check finds no evidence supporting the claim; investigations show that free COVID-19 vaccine distribution in India was based on health-risk prioritization (e.g., healthcare workers, the elderly) under a [special immunization program](https://m.economictimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/healthcare/covid-19-vaccine-will-under-distributed-under-special-immunization-programme-officials/articleshow/78814699.cms), with no conditions linked to voting behavior. Official government policy and the [Co-WIN platform](https://www.mohfw.gov.in/pdf/FAQsCOVID19vaccinesvaccinationprogramWebsiteupload.pdf) specified eligibility by medical criteria, not political affiliation, and even during the 2020 elections, [party pledges](https://www.newsclick.in/Bihar-Elections-BJP-Promises-Free-COVID-19-Vaccines-Opposition-%23-VaccinePolitics) were not implemented as vote-based policies. Therefore, the claim is refuted.
after_justification: The fact-check refutes the claim by showing that while the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) made political statements in October 2020 suggesting free COVID-19 vaccines were for their supporters, India's official vaccination policy was based on public health criteria, not political affiliation. There is no credible evidence of any government policy or implemented scheme that conditioned free vaccination on voting for the BJP, as confirmed by official government communications and fact-checking organizations.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Did any government authority in India (central, state, or local) issue an official policy, order, or directive in 2020 that made free COVID-19 vaccination conditional on voting for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: No, there is no evidence that any Indian government authority issued an official policy, order, or directive making free COVID-19 vaccination conditional on voting for the BJP. The search result states that "The Indian government and BJP announced that only voters supporting the BJP in the 2020 elections would receive the COVID-19 vaccine free of cost," but this refers to political statements or campaign rhetoric rather than a formal, implemented government policy.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Was there any formal or informal communication from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leadership or its representatives in 2020 stating that free COVID-19 vaccines would only be provided to their voters?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Yes, according to The Hindu and India Today, the BJP did state in October 2020 that free COVID vaccines were only for those who vote for them.

adopted_qa_evidence.answer: The search result does not provide credible evidence of such a policy. No official Indian government circulars, meeting minutes, or verified news reports from 2020 confirm any linkage between free COVID-19 vaccine eligibility and voting for the Bharatiya Janata Party. In fact, fact-checking organizations and government communications at the time consistently clarified that the vaccine would be provided based on public health criteria, not political affiliation.

retrieved_evidence.text:
“When the coronavirus vaccine is developed, it will be administered free of cost to the people of the state, with the government bearing all costs,” said Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Edappadi Palaniswami on Thursday, 22 October.
Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, too, announced that the poor people in the state would be given the vaccine free of cost.
The announcements by the two states comes on the same day Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman released the Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) poll manifesto for the upcoming Bihar Assembly elections.
“Since the trials of COVID-19 vaccine have begun in the country, talks were on among the poor sections of the society whether they will be able to afford it.
Let me make it clear that the vaccine in Madhya Pradesh will be provided free of cost to all poor people of the state.
While unveiling the Bihar Election manifesto in Patna, Sitharaman on Thursday had said, “As and when the vaccine candidates that are currently under various levels of trials in the country get scientific clearances and a go-ahead for production, the people of Bihar will get vaccination for free once the production in India is on a large scale.
This is our first poll promise as mentioned in the manifesto.”
The announcement from the Tamil Nadu CM comes at a time when the daily number of COVID-19 cases in Chennai are dipping below 100.
On Wednesday, findings of a serosurvey revealed that nearly one-third of the city’s population has been exposed to the virus.
The Chennai Corporation stated that 6,389 samples were collected randomly across the city, of which 2,062 tested positive for IgG antibodies, which is about 32.3 per cent of the population.
The serosurvey is being conducted to detect the transmission of coronavirus in the society. These population-based surveys are done by performing blood tests on individuals to check if they have developed antibodies to the infection.
The detailed results with ward-wise figures will be announced soon.

NEW DELHI: As a controversy raged over BJP's election manifesto promising free coronavirus vaccine for everyone in Bihar, government officials on Thursday said the vaccine, once ready, will be distributed under a special COVID-19 immunization programme, with the Centre procuring it directly and making it available free-of-cost to all priority groups.
The Centre has started the process of identifying around 30 crore priority beneficiaries who will be given vaccine in the initial phase.
The Centre will procure the vaccine directly and make it available free-of-cost for the priority beneficiaries.
States have been asked not to chart separate pathways of procurement, the officials said.
The existing digital platform and processes used for the Universal Immunisation Programme are being enhanced to track COVID-19 vaccine administration and movement, from procurement to storage to distribution to individual beneficiaries, as and when the vaccine becomes available, the health ministry officials said.
Also, online training modules are being developed for vaccinators.
The government has chalked out four categories which include around one crore healthcare professionals, including doctors, MBBS students and nurses, around two crore frontline workers, including municipal corporation workers, ASHA workers and police personnel, about 26 crore people aged above 50 and those below 50 with co-morbidities.
"A final decision is yet to be taken in this regard," an official said.
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Thursday released the BJP's manifesto for the Bihar assembly polls which promised free COVID-19 vaccine once it has been cleared by the ICMR.
Presently, under the UIP children, adolescents and pregnant women are vaccinated against vaccine-preventable diseases free of cost by the state.

Family Planning Efforts Upended by the Coronavirus
In India and around the world, community health workers are being rerouted to deal with the pandemic—with dangerous results.
On a hot afternoon in April, while the rest of her village stayed home under lockdown, community health worker Urmila Patel walked to a pharmacy to purchase a pregnancy test for a neighbor.
As one of India’s almost 900,000 accredited social health workers, Patel usually focuses on maternal and newborn health.
For hundreds of millions of Indians, these workers—locals who are given basic health care training by the government—are their primary source of information and services related to family planning.

As one of India’s almost 900,000 accredited social health workers, Patel usually focuses on maternal and newborn health.
For hundreds of millions of Indians, these workers—locals who are given basic health care training by the government—are their primary source of information and services related to family planning.
When the Indian government went into overdrive in its fight against the coronavirus, community health workers like Patel, who lives in Maharashtra state, were drafted to the front lines and ordered to mostly replace their usual rounds with coronavirus monitoring.
Since before India’s lockdown began on March 25, Patel has been going door to door daily to offer coronavirus education and screen residents of Surul village for symptoms, referring them to local health centers if needed.
But even as the need for reproductive health services mounts under lockdown, India’s shift in resources has left families empty-handed.
“I continue to distribute contraceptives while carrying out the coronavirus survey, but it isn’t enough.
I can no longer provide the kind of support that I once did,” Patel said.
